final_briefs.title: GSoC Organizations
final_briefs.description: **A searchable directory lets you explore every past Google Summer of Code organization in one place.** The repository curates a list of all GSoC organizations, links to their project pages, and highlights beginner‑friendly “good first issue” tickets. It also includes a step‑by‑step first‑PR walkthrough so newcomers can make their first real contribution without prior GSoC experience.
final_briefs.why_it_matters: Provides a curated, searchable directory of past GSoC organizations, making it fast for engineers to discover real‑world open‑source projects and beginner‑friendly contribution opportunities.
final_briefs.who_cares: Students, early‑career developers, and anyone looking to start contributing to open source through Google Summer of Code.

final_briefs.title: Pre‑flight Checks for USDT (TRC‑20) Transfers on TRON
final_briefs.description: **Run a quick pre‑flight routine to estimate Energy and Bandwidth and avoid OUT_OF_ENERGY failures on TRON.** The guide explains that a USDT transfer consumes two resources—Bandwidth for transaction size and Energy for contract execution—and shows how to calculate the required amounts before signing. By checking the fee_limit and available Energy, developers can prevent costly transaction failures and excess TRX burns.
final_briefs.why_it_matters: Shows how to reliably estimate TRON Energy and Bandwidth before signing a USDT (TRC‑20) transfer, preventing costly OUT_OF_ENERGY failures and excess TRX burn.
final_briefs.who_cares: Blockchain engineers building wallets, payout services, or dApps on the TRON network, especially those handling high‑volume USDT transfers.

final_briefs.title: Vertical Japanese broke my OCR: how I group manga text into speech bubbles on iOS
final_briefs.description: **A three‑pass OCR pipeline groups vertical Japanese manga text into correctly ordered speech bubbles on iOS.** The article details why manga pages challenge standard OCR—vertical columns, many separate bubbles, and tiny glyphs—and describes a solution that runs three concurrent OCR passes, clusters text blocks by geometry, and reorders them to match the right‑to‑left, top‑to‑bottom reading flow.
final_briefs.why_it_matters: Describes a practical pipeline for grouping vertical Japanese manga text into speech bubbles on iOS, turning noisy OCR output into readable, correctly ordered translations.
final_briefs.who_cares: iOS developers, computer‑vision engineers, and product teams creating OCR‑based translation or manga‑reading apps.

final_briefs.title: Context Guardian: helping coding agents understand the impact of a change
final_briefs.description: **Context Guardian maps code changes to affected features, giving AI coding agents a safety net against hidden regressions.** The tool combines a CLI with an AI skill to build a project‑wide code map, match changed files to dependent features, and run configured validation commands. It can also flag platform‑specific counterparts (e.g., iOS vs Android) after a change, integrating with Claude, Gemini, Copilot, and other agents.
final_briefs.why_it_matters: Introduces Context Guardian, a tool that maps code changes to affected features and runs automated checks, helping AI‑assisted coding agents avoid hidden regressions.
final_briefs.who_cares: Teams that rely on AI coding assistants (Claude, Gemini, Copilot, etc.), DevOps engineers, and code‑review automation specialists.
